- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.27) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or near zero (sentiment < 0.18) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term mean reversion toward prior 18-day average.
- When sentiment is high and price is rising, model overweights momentum and fails to adjust for potential reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates late-period price increases (last 7–10 days) when sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment turns negative mid-period, model fails to adjust downward — often underestimates the depth of correction.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trend if sentiment diverges from historical pattern — sentiment history should override pure trend-based forecasting.
